common.tagline: Know what you have, what is already committed, and what the next dollar should do.

landing.headline: Your family’s finances, with one clear answer: what the next dollar should do.
landing.subheadline: Cifraapp brings together your household’s accounts, bills, debts and goals, works out what is actually left, and builds a plan of action every month. A family finance app made for Panama.
landing.seoTitle: Family finance app: know what to do with your money
landing.seoDescription: Cifraapp is the finance app for families: it gathers accounts, bills, debts and goals, works out what is truly available and gives you a plan of action every month. Free to start. Built for Panama.
landing.keywords: family finance app, family budget, household budget, personal finance Panama, family expense tracking, debt payoff plan, family savings, tax reserve for freelancers Panama
landing.proof: Free with up to {transactions} movements a month · No bank connection · Export everything, any time

footer.note: {name} organizes your finances and tells you what to do with your money. It is not a bank, it does not move your money, and it does not replace your accountant. Tax figures are estimates and are called that everywhere in the application.

demo.label: Demonstration
demo.note: Example figures, consistent with each other. None belong to a real person.

try.title: Try it now with your numbers
try.detail: No account and nothing saved. Enter what you have and what you must pay this month, and see what is actually left.
try.availableDetail: of {balance} in accounts, with {committed} already committed and a {buffer} buffer
try.shortDetail: Cifraapp tells you before the first due date, not after.
try.orderTitle: The order it gets covered in
try.free: Free for expensive debt and goals
try.cta: Save these numbers and build my plan
try.ctaHint: When you create your account, the setup assistant starts with these figures already filled in.

capabilities.title: Everything it does for your family
capabilities.detail: Six things done today in your head, on a sheet, or not at all. Demonstration figures, consistent with each other.

import.title: Upload the statement and duplicate nothing
import.detail: PDF, CSV, XLSX or OFX, as your bank hands it over. Every movement gets a fingerprint: upload the same file twice and the second does not go in. Transfers between your own accounts do not count as spending.
import.caption: Four lines of a statement, imported

plan.title: A plan of action every month, line by line
plan.detail: When the salary lands, the plan says where every dollar goes and in what order: overdue, due soon, minimums, tax reserve, buffer, expensive debt, goals. If you disagree with the order, you change it.
plan.caption: A {income} salary on the 15th, allocated
plan.cardWhy: Avoids late fees and extra interest
plan.goalWhy: What remains goes to the first goal
plan.total: The whole salary has a destination

debts.title: Get out of debt with the strategy that saves the most
debts.detail: Compare avalanche against snowball with your real debts, and see in how many months you are free and how much interest you save.
debts.caption: Three debts, {extra} extra a month
debts.saving: With {extra} extra a month: {months} months sooner and {interest} less interest than paying minimums only.

tax.title: If you are self-employed, the tax reserve sets itself aside
tax.detail: Every income sets aside the percentage you choose, from the day it arrives. It is called an estimate because it is one: your accountant has the last word, and it is always named that way here.
tax.caption: One invoice, collected

goals.title: Goals with a number: how much to set aside each month
goals.detail: For every goal, how much you would have to save a month, and what changes if you take on more risk. Modelled with assumptions you can edit. We do not tell you what to invest in: that is regulated advice, and we do not give it.
goals.caption: A {target} goal in {months} months, with {current} already saved
goals.note: At each level’s expected assumption. A level whose horizon is too short is flagged, whatever the arithmetic says.

chat.title: Ask in your own words and get an answer with your figures
chat.detail: The assistant knows your case and answers with the numbers in your records. It rejects any answer that mentions a figure that did not come from there.
chat.caption: A conversation
chat.question: Can I pay off the card in full this month?
chat.answer: Not without dipping below the buffer. You have {available} available and the card owes {card}. If you pay the {minimum} minimum and add {extra}, you stay above the buffer and the card drops to {remaining}.
chat.grounded: Every figure in this answer came from your records

who.title: Who it is for
who.detail: The same engine, three different situations.

couples.title: Couples and families
couples.detail: Finances managed together without losing what belongs to each person. Each person decides what to share and what not to.

independents.title: Independent professionals
independents.detail: Income arrives whole and feels available. The tax reserve sets aside what was never yours, from the day it lands.

accountants.title: Accountants
accountants.detail: Explicit access, scoped and revocable. An accountant never gets access automatically.

pricing.title: Plans
pricing.detail: A free plan that is genuinely useful. Prices and limits come from the database: they are the same ones the product enforces.

refusals.title: What this product refuses to do
refusals.detail: Almost everything below is a decision not to do something that would have been easier.

duplicates.claim: It never imports the same transaction twice
duplicates.detail: Every movement has a fingerprint computed from the account, the date, the amount and the normalized description. Upload the same statement again and nothing happens.

transfers.claim: Your card payment does not count as spending
transfers.detail: Moving money between your own accounts is not spending. Counting it would double every purchase already on the card and make a disciplined month look like a disaster.

ai.detail: It explains and classifies; it does not compute. Every figure comes from your records, and the system rejects any answer that mentions a number we did not give it.

tax.detail: We say estimated tax reserve, with the version of the rules that produced it. Panama’s rules live in the database, with their source, and are not shown until somebody qualified has reviewed them.

close.title: Your family deserves to know what to do with its money, not just how much it has.
close.detail: Start for free, with this month’s numbers. If you ever leave, you take everything with you.

mechanism.basis: of {liquid} in accounts, with {committed} already committed

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.detail: The same limits the product enforces. This table is read from the database, not from a list maintained separately.

empty.title: The plan catalogue is not loaded yet
empty.body: Prices are read from the database. With no active plans, this page invents none.

notes.title: Before you decide
notes.provisional: These figures are provisional: final pricing is not decided and this is not an offer.
notes.freeTier: The free plan is not a trial. If a subscription lapses your account returns to it, and your history stays yours.
notes.noLockIn: You can export everything inside as CSV and JSON, at any time, without asking.

blog.title: Writing
blog.detail: About money decisions, and about how this is built.

empty.title: We haven't published anything yet
empty.body: When there is something worth reading it will appear here. An empty list beats three filler articles.

empty.title: No entries yet
empty.body: What gets published here is what changed for someone using the product, not every commit.

legal.unreviewed: This text is a draft and has not been reviewed by a lawyer. It is published so you can see what it says today, not as a settled document.

missing.title: This document is not published yet
missing.body: We would rather show nothing than show a legal text nobody wrote.

signIn.title: Sign in to your system
signIn.detail: Your accounts, your rules, and your allocation plan.

signUp.title: Create your account
signUp.detail: The account first; your household and bank accounts come next.
signUp.checkYourEmail: We sent you an email to confirm your address. Open it to finish creating your account.

forgot.title: Recover your password
forgot.detail: We'll send you a link to choose a new one. It expires in an hour.
forgot.sent: If that address has an account, the link is on its way. Check your email, including spam.
forgot.rateLimited: We can't send another email right now. Wait up to an hour, or use a recovery link that already arrived in your inbox (check spam).

reset.title: Choose a new password
reset.detail: Saving it ends every other session open on your account.
reset.expiredBody: Recovery links expire after an hour and can only be used once. Request a new one.

errors.title: We couldn't continue
errors.signInFailed: That email and password don't match. Check them and try again.
errors.signUpFailed: We couldn't create the account. Please try again in a moment.
errors.passwordTooShort: The password needs at least 8 characters.
errors.linkExpired: That link has expired. Request a new one.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

mfa.title: Second step
mfa.detail: Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app. It submits on its own when complete.

errors.codeRejected: That code is not valid or has expired. Wait for the next one in the app and try again.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

onboarding.title: Let's start with your household
onboarding.detail: A household groups the finances that are managed together. It can be just you, a couple, or a family. You decide what gets shared afterwards.

fields.name: Household name
fields.nameHint: Your name, for instance, or yours and your partner's.

errors.title: We couldn't create the household
errors.createFailed: We couldn't create the household. Please try again in a moment.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Please sign in again.

overview.title: Your position

gauge.label: Safe to spend
gauge.explanation: The level falls when you commit money and rises only when money actually arrives. Everything above the surface already belongs to something.

stats.liquidDetail: The sum of your liquid accounts: current, savings, cash and wallets.
stats.committedDetail: Upcoming obligations, minimum debt payments, the tax reserve and your buffer.

empty.title: Give your money somewhere to live.
empty.body: Add your first account or import a statement. From there we work out what is committed and what is genuinely left.

claims.title: What claims that money
claims.detail: Commitments in the next 30 days, ordered by due date.
claims.emptyTitle: Nothing committed in the next 30 days.
claims.emptyBody: Once you record a recurring obligation it appears here and lowers what is available.

overview.planLink: See what to do with this money
overview.scopeNote: This is the same figure the plan shows: your liquid balance less the next 30 days of obligations, your minimum debt payments, the estimated tax reserve and your minimum buffer. The plan tells you what to do with it.

plan.title: What to do with this money
plan.detail: A concrete plan for the money you have available right now, line by line, with the reason for each.
plan.basis: This plan allocates {incoming} of liquid balance. When new money arrives, the same calculation runs against that income.

empty.title: There is nothing to allocate yet.
empty.body: Add an account, record an obligation or a debt. With that we can already tell you where each dollar should go.

safeToSpend.title: What is genuinely available
safeToSpend.detail: The balance less everything already spoken for, in the order it gets covered.
safeToSpend.label: Safe to spend
safeToSpend.emptyBody: Once you record an obligation, a debt or a goal, it shows up here and lowers what stays free.

lines.title: The allocation
lines.detail: Top to bottom. Each line takes what it can from what is left.
lines.emptyBody: With no obligations, debts or goals recorded, the whole balance is free.

reason.nothingLeft: Nothing left for {label} from this money.
reason.overdueEssential: Allocate {amount} to {label} because it was due on {due} and is already late.
reason.overdueEssentialWithFee: Puts {amount} toward {label}: it was due on {due} and the {fee} late charge can still be avoided.
reason.upcomingEssential: Allocate {amount} to {label} because it is due on {due}.
reason.upcomingEssentialWithFee: Puts {amount} toward {label}: it is due on {due} and paying it late costs {fee}.
reason.debtMinimum: Allocate {amount} to {label} to cover its minimum payment.
reason.taxReserve: Set aside {amount} as an estimated tax reserve. Confirm it with your accountant.
reason.emergencyFund: Allocate {amount} to {label} because the buffer comes before anything optional.
reason.highInterestDebt: Allocate {amount} to {label} because it carries the highest rate at {apr}%.
reason.expensiveDebt: Allocate {amount} to {label} because it is the most expensive debt you hold.
reason.goalByDate: Allocate {amount} to {label}, which you want ready by {due}.
reason.discretionary: {amount} is yours to spend as of {today}.
reason.partial: That is part of the {requested} it needs.

notes.paused: Contributions to {target} are paused by one of your rules.
notes.otherCurrency: A rule for {target} is written in another currency and was skipped.
notes.marked: {label} is marked {priority} by one of your rules.
notes.taxesFirst: Taxes are reserved before anything else, by one of your rules.
notes.unreachableTarget: A rule points at {target}, which is not somewhere money can go.

raised.percentOfIncoming: Your rule raises {label} to {percent}% of this money.

added.percentOfIncoming: Your rule adds {label} at {percent}% of this money.

debtOrder.title: Which debt to attack
debtOrder.detail: The order your strategy imposes. The extra goes to the first; the others keep paying their minimum.

copilot.title: Reading the plan
copilot.detail: A written summary over the same figures shown above.
copilot.disclaimer: Written by an assistant over the plan already computed. The figures come from your records, not from the assistant.

declined.budget: The assistant reached this month's usage limit. The plan above is complete without it.
declined.quality: The assistant returned something we could not check against your figures, so we did not show it. Every line of the plan explains its own reason.
declined.error: The assistant did not answer. The plan above does not depend on it.

plan.scopeNote: The plan is computed from the accounts, obligations, debts and goals you have recorded today. The tax reserve is an estimate from the rate you configured, not a calculation of tax owed.

reports.title: Statements
reports.detail: {start} to {end}. Every figure comes from your transactions; nothing is summarized or estimated.

empty.title: Nothing to report yet
empty.body: Statements are computed from your transactions. Import a bank statement and these fill themselves in.

income.title: Income and expenses
income.detail: For the period. Movements between your own accounts do not count as spending.
income.transfersExcluded: {count} movements between your own accounts were excluded. A card payment is not an expense: that spending is already in the purchases.
income.emptyBody: Import a statement and confirm its lines. Income and spending group themselves by category.

cashFlow.title: Cash flow
cashFlow.detail: What the period opened with, what came in, what left, and what it closed with.

health.title: Financial health
health.detail: Each component shows the figure it comes from. If you disagree with it, you can see exactly what with.
health.notACreditScore: This score is ours and measures only what you see above. It is not a credit score and no lender uses it.

export.title: Export
export.detail: The same rows you see here, in a file. Amounts are unformatted so a spreadsheet reads them as numbers.

reports.scopeNote: Statements are computed on demand from your transactions and never stored as a copy. A correction to an old movement moves every later balance with it.

accountant.title: Accountant portal

clients.title: Your clients
clients.detail: Every household that granted you access, with what needs attention today.

empty.title: Nobody has granted you access yet
empty.body: An accountant never gains access automatically. When a household grants it, they appear here with the scope they chose.

client.revocable: This access can be revoked at any time and without notice. When that happens, this page stops existing for you on the next request.

attention.title: What needs attention
attention.detail: What the household left outstanding, not a task list of your own.

notes.title: Notes
notes.detail: Visible to the household. This is not a private space.

empty.title: No notes
empty.body: A note about a specific transaction is more useful attached to it than loose in a list.

accountant.scopeNote: You only see what each household granted: their accounts, movements, documents and tax situation. Never who their members are, what plan they pay for, or what they asked the assistant.

errors.notFoundBody: The link may be broken, or the page may have moved.
errors.genericBody: We couldn't complete that. Please try again in a moment.

documents.title: Documents and imports
documents.detail: Upload a statement as CSV or OFX. We read every line and tell you how many are new, how many were already there, and which ones need you to look.

form.fileHint: CSV or OFX. Up to 15 MB.

errors.tooLarge: The file is over 15 MB. Export a shorter date range.
errors.unsupportedType: We read CSV and OFX for now. Export the statement in one of those formats.
errors.alreadyImported: You already imported this exact file. Nothing was created, so your transactions are not duplicated.
errors.storageUnavailable: We couldn't store the file. Please try again in a moment.
errors.noAccount: Add an account for these transactions to belong to first.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errors.queueUnavailable: We could not queue the file. Try again in a moment.

form.account: Which account is this statement for?
form.accountHint: Filing a statement against the wrong account is worse than not filing it.
form.queuedDetail: We are reading it. It usually takes a few seconds; a long PDF takes a little more.

history.title: Earlier imports
history.empty: You haven't imported a file yet.

documents.note: Analyzing a file does not create transactions yet. Every line gets a verdict and you confirm before anything enters your records.

noAccount.title: The account these belong to is missing
noAccount.body: A movement has to live in an account. Create yours and come back; it takes under a minute.

review.detail: From {account}, read on {when}. Tick what you want filed.
review.counts: {new} new · {duplicate} possible duplicates · {review} to check · {rejected} we could not read
review.discardConfirm: It closes without filing anything. The file is kept.
review.filed: Filed {count} movements. They count in your statements now.
review.settled: Every line in this file has already been filed.
review.scopeNote: Only what you tick is filed. A filed line keeps its origin: you can trace it back to the file it came from.

hints.new: We found nothing like it in your records.
hints.duplicate: It looks like a movement you already have.
hints.review: It resembles something you have, but not enough for us to decide for you.
hints.rejected: The line had no readable date or amount.

errors.notFound: We could not find this import.
errors.nothingSelected: Tick at least one line before filing.
errors.nothingFiled: Nothing you ticked was still waiting to be filed.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

accounts.title: Your accounts
accounts.detail: Where your money lives and what you owe. Everything else in the system is calculated from this.
accounts.scopeNote: The balance is the one you state: what your bank says today. The movements you import are the detail of how it got there, and they do not change this number on their own.

summary.liquidDetail: The sum of your current, savings, cash and wallet accounts.
summary.owedDetail: Cards, loans and mortgages, held positive.

empty.title: Start with one account.
empty.body: The account your pay lands in is usually the first. With its balance we can already tell you what is committed and what is left.

list.title: Accounts on record
list.detail: You can adjust a balance whenever you check it against your bank.
list.archiveConfirm: It stops counting in your position. Its movements are kept.

form.name: Account name
form.nameHint: However you recognise it. For example, "Banco General current".
form.balanceHintAsset: What you have in that account right now.
form.balanceHintDebt: What you owe, as a positive number. No minus sign.
form.maskHint: Optional, to recognise it. We never store the full number.

errors.title: We could not save the account
errors.nameRequired: Write a name you will recognise the account by.
errors.balanceInvalid: Write the balance as a number. For example, 1250.40
errors.maskInvalid: Digits only in the last four numbers.
errors.typeInvalid: Choose an account type from the list.
errors.createFailed: We could not create the account. Try again in a moment.
errors.notFound: We could not find this account.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

setup.title: Tell us how you live
setup.detail: Six short questions. With them we build your first plan today, without waiting for you to import a statement. You can skip any of them and come back later.
setup.errorTitle: We could not save your answers

error.invalid: Check the amounts: they go as numbers, for example 1250.40
error.saveFailed: We could not save. Try again in a moment.
error.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.
error.dependentsExceedMembers: More people cannot depend on the income than live in the house.

household.title: Who lives in the house?
household.detail: By name. How many people the money has to reach changes everything we tell you afterwards.
household.name: Name
household.nameHint: What you call them at home.
household.dependent: Depends on the household income (brings in none of their own)
household.empty: Nobody on the list yet. Add at least yourself: how many people the money has to reach changes everything we tell you afterwards.

income.title: What comes in, and how often?
income.detail: Salaries, fees, rent. If you work for yourself and the amount moves, mark it as approximate: the plan treats it differently.
income.name: Where it comes from
income.approximateHint: Tick it if it changes month to month. We will not use this figure as if it were fixed.
income.empty: No income yet. Add the first one — a salary, fees, rent you collect — or skip this step if nothing is coming in right now.

savings.title: What do you have today?
savings.detail: Your account balances and your savings. It is the starting point the plan allocates from.
savings.name: Account name
savings.institutionHint: Where the account is held. It is what lets us recognise your statements when you upload them.
savings.rateHint: As your statement reports it. Leave it blank if you do not know: we will not invent one.
savings.empty: No accounts yet. Add the first one with today’s balance: it is the starting point the plan divides up.
savings.totalDetail: The sum of what you just typed. We do not store it: it is here so you can see the figure your accounts make before moving on.
savings.totalUnpriced: {count} still has no price. That value is not added in here yet.

commitments.title: What do you have to pay every month?
commitments.detail: Rent, power, water, school, internet. This is what turns a balance into "what is actually left".
commitments.name: What you pay
commitments.essentialHint: What you would pay even in a bad month. The plan covers it first.
commitments.deductedFrom: Is it taken out of a salary?
commitments.deductedFromHint: If it comes off the payslip before you are paid, say so here. That way we know the money never reached you.
commitments.deductedFromChosenHint: We take it off that salary, not off your balance. If the figure you entered under Income already has this deduction taken out, leave it as it is.
commitments.empty: No payments yet. Add the first one — rent, electricity, school — or skip this step if you have no fixed payments.
commitments.lateFeeHint: If paying it late costs more, say so here. It tells us which one is least worth delaying.
commitments.lateFeeAfterHint: Days after the due date before the charge applies. If they charge from day one, put 0.

debts.title: Do you owe anything?
debts.detail: Cards, loans, a mortgage. With the rate we can tell you which to attack first and what that order saves you.
debts.name: Who you owe
debts.aprHint: It is on your statement. If you do not know it, leave it blank and add it later.
debts.minimumHint: The least you have to pay each month.
debts.limitHint: Only if it is a credit card. It is how we know what you still have available; leave it blank for a loan.
debts.holderHint: Pick who in the household it belongs to. Leave it as is if it is shared.
debts.available: That leaves {amount} available on this card.
debts.empty: No debts yet. Add the first one — a card, a loan — or skip this step if you owe nothing.

goals.title: What is all this for?
goals.detail: An emergency fund, a trip, a deposit on a house. Without a goal, the money left over has nowhere to go.
goals.name: What you want to reach
goals.dateHint: Optional. With a date, the plan works out how much to set aside each month.
goals.bufferHint: The balance you never want to go below. The plan protects it before anything optional.
goals.empty: No goals yet. Add the first one: without a goal the plan divides what is left over without knowing where it is going.

draft.notice: We loaded the figures you tried on the home page. Fix whatever does not fit.

review.title: Review what you told us
review.detail: The same six questions, filled in with what is on record. Correct whatever needs it: saving updates what is there rather than adding a copy beside it.
review.notice: Anything you take out here is archived, not deleted: it stays in your history and you can bring it back from its own screen.

holdings.title: Shares, funds and crypto
holdings.detail: If you hold shares or coins, put them here. We look the price up as you type and track what they are worth and how they move. You state how much you hold; the market states the price, with its time.
holdings.symbolHint: Type the name or the symbol and pick it from the list. That way «BTC», which is a fund, is never mistaken for Bitcoin.
holdings.quantityHint: Shares or coins. Decimals are fine: 0.35 of a bitcoin is valid.
holdings.unknown: We could not find that symbol. Check the spelling — BTC-USD, for instance, rather than BTC.
holdings.unavailable: We could not reach the price just now. You can carry on; we will try again later.
holdings.searchEmptyHint: Try the full name — bitcoin, apple, vanguard — or drop the type filter.
holdings.searchError: We could not reach the search just now.
holdings.searchErrorHint: That is our problem, not yours. Retry, or type the exact symbol and carry on.

errors.generic: Something failed while saving. Try again.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again and we will save it.
errors.notFound: This no longer exists. Someone may have removed it from another device.
errors.createFailed: Could not create it. Try again.
errors.invalid: Something is missing, or a value we could not read.
errors.nameRequired: Give it a name you will recognise.
errors.targetInvalid: Write how much you want to save.
errors.savedInvalid: Write how much you have saved. If nothing yet, put 0.
errors.limitInvalid: Write the card limit, or leave it empty.
errors.bufferInvalid: Write the buffer, or leave it empty.
errors.aprInvalid: Write the annual rate, for example 24.5
errors.parentIsSelf: A category cannot sit inside itself.
errors.accountRequired: Choose the account the money came from.
errors.splitInvalid: Check the parts: each one needs an amount.
errors.splitDoesNotSum: The parts have to add up to exactly the movement's amount.
errors.importedCannotDelete: This movement came from a statement and is not deleted. You can exclude it so it stops counting.
errors.factInvalid: Choose a fact from the list.
errors.valueInvalid: The value does not match that fact's type.
errors.targetRequired: Write what the rule points at.
errors.ruleInvalid: The rule is not valid. Check the condition and the action.
errors.nothingToAccept: There is no plan to accept yet.
errors.alreadyStarted: It already started processing and cannot be cancelled.
errors.horizonInvalid: Choose how many months to look ahead.
errors.monthsInvalid: Write a valid number of months.
errors.changeIsEmpty: A scenario with no cost and no income is doing nothing under another name.
errors.bandIncomplete: If you change the assumptions, give all three: poor, expected and good.
errors.bandOutOfOrder: The poor assumption cannot exceed the expected one, nor the expected the good one.
errors.symbolInvalid: Write the symbol the way TradingView does. For example, NASDAQ:AAPL or TVC:GOLD.
errors.alreadyWatching: That symbol is already on your list.

movements.title: Movements
movements.detail: Everything that came in and went out, with the category we gave it. This is where you fix it.

filters.title: Filter
filters.queryHint: Any part of the text that appears on the statement.
filters.activeNote: You are seeing a subset. The totals above are of what is filtered.

uncategorizedBanner.title: {count} movements with no category
uncategorizedBanner.body: With no category they enter no budget and no statement. Categorising them is what makes every other figure mean something.

empty.title: No movements yet.
empty.body: Import a statement and they will appear here, or record by hand the cash expense no bank ever saw.

noResults.title: No movement matches.
noResults.body: Try fewer filters or a wider date range.

movement.title: Movement

notFound.title: That movement does not exist.
notFound.body: It may have been removed, or the link belongs to another household.

movement.original: As it came on the statement

category.title: Category
category.detail: Changing it here also teaches the system, and records who changed it.

splits.title: Split across categories
splits.detail: One purchase can be two things. The parts have to add up to exactly the amount.

note.title: Note
note.detail: So you remember what it was for, when you look at it in three months.

status.title: How it counts
status.detail: Excluding deletes nothing: the movement stays and stops counting toward your figures.
status.markTransfer: This is a transfer between my own accounts

history.title: What has been changed
history.detail: Every category change is recorded. That is what makes an automatic classification undoable.

remove.title: Remove
remove.detail: Only the ones you recorded by hand are removed. Imported ones are excluded.
remove.confirm: It is removed and the account balance goes back.

movementNew.title: Record an expense
movementNew.detail: Cash, the lunch place, the taxi: what appears on no statement.
movementNew.why: If you do not record it, the system thinks you spend less than you do, and tells you that you have more available than you have.
movementNew.accountHint: That account's balance goes down by this expense.
movementNew.descriptionHint: The way you would say it. For example, «lunch with Ana».
movementNew.categoryHint: Optional. You can set it later.

noAccounts.title: You need an account first.
noAccounts.body: An expense comes from somewhere. Create the account where you keep the cash and come back.

income.title: Your income
income.detail: What comes in, how often, and when the next one lands. Everything the plan can allocate starts here.

summary.monthlyDetail: Each income brought to its monthly equivalent and added up.

list.title: Recorded income
list.detail: Correct an amount when it changes. The gap between what you said and what arrives is a fact worth having.

income.removeConfirm: It stops counting in the plan. What already happened is kept.

empty.title: No income recorded yet.
empty.body: The salary that lands is the first one. With that, the plan can already tell you what to do with the next dollar.

form.name: Which income is it?
form.nameHint: The way you call it. For example, «Ana's salary» or «Apartment rent».
form.amountHint: What you actually receive, not what the contract says.
form.nextHint: Leave it empty and we work it out from the frequency.
form.approximateHint: «About 2,400 in a good month» and «2,400 on the 15th» are two different claims, and the plan is entitled to know which one it was told.

frequencies.semimonthly: Twice a month (15th and month end)

debts.title: Your debts
debts.detail: How much you owe, at what rate, and what has to be paid this month. The rate is what decides which one to attack first.

summary.minimumsDetail: What has to be paid to stay out of arrears.

list.title: Recorded debts
list.detail: Ordered from the most expensive rate to the cheapest, which is the order worth attacking them in.

debts.removeConfirm: It leaves the plan and the simulator. What you already paid is kept.

empty.title: No debts recorded.
empty.body: If you carry a card balance or a loan, record it with its rate: that is the number that decides what every extra dollar should do.

form.name: Which debt is it?
form.nameHint: The way you recognise it. For example, «Banco General Visa».
form.balance: How much do you owe today?
form.balanceHint: Positive. Do not use a minus sign.
form.aprHint: The number shown as APR or annual interest on your statement.
form.dueDayHint: The day of the month it falls due.
form.limitHint: Optional. It tells you how much of the limit you are using.

debt.title: Debt

notFound.title: That debt does not exist.
notFound.body: It may have been removed, or the link belongs to another household.

stats.paidDetail: Against the balance you first recorded.
stats.monthlyInterestDetail: What not paying it costs, on today's balance.

payoff.title: When it ends
payoff.detail: Worked out from the payment you make, on today's balance and rate. No new charges.
payoff.never: Never. The minimum does not even cover the interest.
payoff.simulate: See what happens if I pay more

debt.noLimit: You did not record a limit for this debt.

goals.title: Your goals
goals.detail: What you are saving toward, how much you have, and by when. The plan sends what is left over here.

summary.savedDetail: What you recorded on each goal, added up.

list.title: Recorded goals
list.detail: Ordered by what you said matters first.

goals.removeConfirm: It is marked abandoned. It is kept so you know it existed.

empty.title: No goals yet.
empty.body: The emergency fund is usually the first: three months of expenses, so a surprise does not become a debt.

form.name: What do you want to reach?
form.nameHint: Concrete. «Emergency fund» or «Trip to Spain in July».
form.dateHint: Optional. With a date we can tell you how much to save each month.

notFound.title: That goal does not exist.
notFound.body: It may have been removed, or the link belongs to another household.

stats.monthly: Per month to arrive on time
stats.monthlyDetail: What is missing, spread across the months left.

progress.title: Progress
progress.label: Saved against the target
progress.noDate: Without a target date we cannot tell you how much to save each month. Set one and we will work it out.
progress.late: The date has passed and {amount} is still missing.
progress.reached: Goal reached. Mark it as reached, or raise the target.

commitments.title: This month's commitments
commitments.detail: Rent, the light bill, the school. This is what makes your balance not what you have.

summary.totalDetail: What already has an owner before you decide anything.

list.title: Recorded commitments
list.detail: Ordered by the next one falling due.

commitments.removeConfirm: It stops being subtracted from what is available.

empty.title: No commitments recorded yet.
empty.body: Rent or the mortgage is usually the first. Without this, «available» is just your balance, and your balance lies.

form.name: What do you pay?
form.nameHint: The way you call it. For example, «Rent» or «Mateo's school».
form.day: What day of the month is it due?
form.dayHint: Put 31 and in a short month we move it to the last day.
form.essentialHint: Tick this if not paying it has serious consequences. The plan protects it before anything else.
form.categoryHint: Optional. It lets real spending be matched against this commitment.

categories.title: Spending categories
categories.detail: The vocabulary your household uses for where money goes. Change it until it sounds like you.

list.title: Your categories
list.detail: The ones the system ships can be renamed. The ones you create can be removed while they have no movements.

categories.removeConfirm: With movements behind it, it is archived instead of deleted, so your statements are not rewritten.

empty.title: No categories yet.
empty.body: Create the first with the name you actually use. «Groceries» and «Eating out» are usually the two that carry the most.

form.name: Category name
form.nameHint: The way you say it, not the way an accountant would.
form.kindHint: Decides whether it counts as spending. A transfer between your own accounts is not an expense.
form.parentHint: Optional. A category inside another inherits its type.

people.title: Who lives here
people.detail: How many people the money has to reach. A thousand dollars left over is not the same fact for one person as for five.

summary.dependentsDetail: Those who bring in no income of their own.

list.title: People in the household
list.detail: Those who contribute first, then those who depend.

people.removeConfirm: They leave the list and the household counts.

empty.title: The list is not filled in yet.
empty.body: Start with yourself. With the full list, every explanation we give you knows how many people the money has to reach.

form.name: Name
form.nameHint: What you call them at home.
form.dependentHint: Tick this if they bring in no income of their own.
form.yearHint: Optional. The year only: we have no use for the day and month.

people.syncNote: This list is what counts. The number the plan uses updates itself whenever you change it.

settings.title: Household settings
settings.detail: Four decisions that change a figure you read every day.

form.name: Household name
form.nameHint: What you call it between you.
form.bufferHint: The floor «available» refuses to go below. It is why the plan says one figure and not your whole balance.
form.strategyHint: Decides which balance the extra dollar attacks.
form.taxRateHint: What you set aside from each invoice if you work for yourself. Leave it empty if it does not apply.

strategies.custom: My way — I decide the order

settings.strategyNote: Avalanche costs you less money. Snowball is the one more people finish. The product has an opinion and does not decide for you.

currency.title: Currency
currency.detail: The household currency is not changed. Every stored figure carries its code, and changing it would reinterpret everything stored without converting any of it.

profile.title: The household
profile.stated: You stated {count} people in the questionnaire

danger.title: The questionnaire
danger.detail: You can answer it again. It erases nothing you already recorded.

security.title: Security
security.detail: Two-step verification with an authenticator app, such as Google Authenticator. Once on, signing in asks for the password and a code.
security.enabledDetail: Every time you sign in, after the password we will ask for the code from your app.
security.disabledDetail: With only a password, whoever has it can see everything here. A second step stops that.
security.scanTitle: Scan this code with your app
security.scanDetail: Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password or any app that uses TOTP codes. Then enter the code it shows.
security.secretLabel: Or type this key by hand
security.confirmed: Two-step verification is on. From now on, signing in asks for the code.
security.disableDetail: To confirm it is you, enter the current code from your app. Afterwards, signing in asks only for the password.

errors.codeRejected: That code is not valid or has expired. Wait for the next one and try again.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.
errors.generic: Something failed. Nothing changed; try again.

importJob.title: Reading your statement

notFound.title: We could not find that run.
notFound.body: It may have finished long ago, or the link belongs to another household.

importJob.queued: Queued. It starts in a few seconds.

stages.matching: Checking for repeats against what you already have

importJob.retrying: Attempt {attempt} of {max}. The last one failed and we are trying again.
importJob.failedTitle: We could not read this file
importJob.cancelled: Cancelled. The file is still stored.
importJob.leaveNote: You can close this page. The work carries on and waits for you under «Import».

review.title: To review
review.detail: What the system noticed and will not decide on its own. Everything here is your call.

empty.title: Nothing is waiting for you.
empty.body: When you import a statement, whatever the system notices shows up here: repeats, transfers, expenses that recur, and categories it is unsure about.

duplicates.title: Possible repeats
duplicates.detail: Movements that look like the same one twice.

transfers.title: Transfers to confirm
transfers.detail: Money that moved between your own accounts and should not count as spending.

recurring.title: Expenses that repeat
recurring.detail: Patterns we detected that could be commitments.

categories.title: Categories to confirm
categories.detail: Movements we classified without much confidence.

review.rescanDetail: Runs the four analyses over your movements again.
review.rescanQueued: Analysis queued. Anything new shows up in a few seconds.

duplicates.title: Possible repeats
duplicates.detail: The same expense can arrive twice: in two statements, or because you recorded it by hand and then imported it.

empty.title: No repeats waiting.
empty.body: When the system sees two movements that look like the same one, it asks you here before touching anything.

duplicates.sameNote: The second stops counting. It is not deleted.

transfersReview.title: Transfers to confirm
transfersReview.detail: Moving $500 from your account to your savings is not spending and not income. Counted as both, every figure you have goes wrong.

empty.title: Nothing to confirm.
empty.body: When we see two equal and opposite movements between your accounts, we ask you here.

transfersReview.cardPaymentNote: The purchases that produced that balance already counted as spending when you made them. Counting the payment as well would count them twice.
transfersReview.confirm: Yes, that is my own transfer
transfersReview.reject: No, they are two different things

recurringReview.title: Expenses that repeat
recurringReview.detail: Patterns we saw in your movements. Confirming one turns it into a commitment the plan accounts for.

empty.title: No new patterns detected.
empty.body: It takes at least three appearances to call something recurring. With a couple of months of movements they start to show up.

categoryReview.title: Categories to confirm
categoryReview.detail: The system classified these without much confidence. We would rather ask you than put a doubtful figure in your budget.

empty.title: Nothing doubtful right now.
empty.body: When the system is unsure of a category it does not apply it silently: it asks you here.

categoryReview.acceptNote: Whatever you choose becomes yours, and no rule overwrites it afterwards.

merchants.title: Merchants
merchants.detail: Where the money actually goes. Setting the category once here stops the question being asked thirty times.

list.title: Recognised merchants
list.detail: The category you set applies to that merchant's movements you have not categorised yourself.

merchants.removeConfirm: The movements keep their category. Only the merchant label is lost.

empty.title: No merchants yet.
empty.body: They are recognised on their own when you import statements. When they appear, you decide each one's category here.

form.name: Merchant name
form.nameHint: The way you call it, not the way it reads on the statement.
form.categoryHint: Applies to anything you have not categorised yourself.

budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.detail: How much you mean to spend on each category, against what you have spent and what is still to pay this month.

summary.projected: At this pace you end at

list.title: Your budgets
list.detail: A monthly budget with no end date recomputes itself each month.

budgets.removeConfirm: The budget and its lines are removed. Your movements do not change.

empty.title: No budget yet.
empty.body: We can build one from what you actually spend: the median of each category over recent months. It is a figure you recognise, and can then argue with.

form.name: Name
form.endsHint: Leave it empty and it renews itself each month.

budgets.suggest: Build one from what I spend
budgets.suggestDetail: Takes the median of each category over the last six months. It never overwrites a figure you set.

notFound.title: That budget does not exist.
notFound.body: It may have been removed, or the link belongs to another household.

stats.committedDetail: Commitments falling due inside the period that you have not paid.
stats.projectedDetail: Projected to the end of the period, from the spending so far.

lines.title: Categories
lines.detail: The amount left already subtracts what you still have to pay this period.
lines.removeConfirm: It leaves the budget. Your movements do not change.

empty.title: This budget has no categories.
empty.body: Add the first one: groceries is usually the one that moves most.

shape.title: How the month was spent
shape.detail: Each bar is a day. It shows whether spending was even or bunched up.

advice.title: This month's advice
advice.detail: What to do with your money this month, in order. Every line comes from a figure you can go and look at.

steps.title: In this order
steps.coverBuffer: You are {amount} short of covering what is already committed. Before anything else, this is the hole to fill.
steps.payOverdue: You have {count} overdue commitment(s). Paying them first is the cheapest thing you can do today.
steps.attackDebt: Send {amount} to {name}. It is the most expensive debt you have, at {apr}% a year, and every month costs more.
steps.fundGoal: Send {amount} to «{name}». You have no expensive debt outstanding, so this is the best destination.
steps.trimBudget: In «{budget}» you are on pace to spend {projected} against {planned} planned. There is still month left to fix it.
steps.nothingLeft: There is nothing free to allocate this month. That is not an error: it is what your figures say.
steps.allClear: Nothing is urgent. What is left is yours to decide.

copilot.title: In words
copilot.detail: Written on the same figures above. If something does not add up, trust the figure, not the paragraph.
copilot.unavailable: The copilot is not switched on in this installation. The figures above are exact regardless: the engine computes them, not the model.
copilot.budget: This month's assistant budget is spent. The figures are unaffected.
copilot.quality: The assistant could not answer without inventing a figure, so it did not answer.
copilot.error: We could not reach the assistant. The figures are still exact.
copilot.disclaimer: Written by an assistant over figures already computed. The numbers come from your records, not from the assistant.

empty.title: There is not enough yet to advise you.
empty.body: Record an account and what is already committed. With that we can tell you what the next dollar should do.

advice.openPlan: See the plan line by line

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.detail: What will go wrong if nothing changes. Each one comes from your own figures.

empty.title: Nothing to tell you.
empty.body: When something is heading the wrong way — a category running hot, an overdue commitment, a card near its limit — we say so here.

kinds.bufferNegative: You are {amount} short of covering what is already committed this month.
kinds.overdueCommitment: «{name}» is past due and still unpaid: {amount}.
kinds.budgetPace: In «{budget}» you are on pace to spend {projected} against {planned} planned.
kinds.highUtilization: «{name}» is at {percent}% of its limit. Above 30% it starts to cost you.
kinds.goalLate: «{name}» is past its date and {amount} is still missing.
kinds.reviewBacklog: You have {count} decisions waiting under «To review».
kinds.uncategorized: {count} movements with no category. Without one they enter no budget.
kinds.categorySpike: You spent {percent}% more on «{category}»: {amount} against the usual {usual}.

debtSimulator.title: Debt simulator
debtSimulator.detail: How long it takes and what it costs in interest, by strategy and by what you put in each month.

form.monthly: How much can you pay each month?
form.monthlyHint: Minimums included. Yours add up to {minimums}.

result.title: With that payment
result.never: At that amount the debt never ends. It does not even cover the interest.
result.belowMinimums: That amount does not cover the minimums. You need at least {required}.
result.noDebts: You have no debts recorded. Nothing to simulate, which is the best possible news.

compare.title: Avalanche against snowball
compare.detail: With the same monthly payment. Avalanche costs you less money; snowball is the one more people finish.
compare.same: With today's debts, both strategies come out the same.
compare.snowballSooner: Snowball finishes {count} months sooner with this combination.

order.title: In what order
order.detail: Under the chosen strategy, and why each one sits where it does.

debtSimulator.note: On today's balance and rate, with no new purchases. If you keep using the card, the result changes.

planHistory.title: Plan tracking
planHistory.detail: What you decided, kept as you saw it. Without this, «did I do what I decided last month?» has no answer.
planHistory.accepted: Plan saved. It is a decision now, not a suggestion.
planHistory.acceptDetail: Saved exactly as you are seeing it. It is not recomputed afterwards.

empty.title: You have not accepted a plan yet.
empty.body: When you accept one it is kept with its lines, and next month you can compare it against what actually happened.

planHistory.compliance: You followed {percent}% of what you planned
planHistory.complianceDetail: Comparing what was allocated to each debt and goal against what actually moved afterwards.
planHistory.notMeasurable: There are not enough movements after this plan yet to measure it.

rules.title: Your rules
rules.detail: «When this happens, do that.» Stored as data, never as code: a rule cannot reach anything outside this list of facts.

list.title: Active rules
list.detail: Evaluated every time the plan is built, in priority order.

rules.removeConfirm: It stops being evaluated. Plans that used it are kept.

empty.title: No rules yet.
empty.body: A typical one: «when the card goes above 30% of its limit, send it 20% of what is left over».

form.name: Rule name
form.explanationHint: Shown verbatim when the rule changes a plan. A rule nobody can explain cannot be reviewed.
form.factHint: These facts only. The list is the limit of what a rule can see.
form.targetHint: What it points at. For example, «debt:visa» or «goal:emergency».
form.actionValueHint: A percentage, an amount, or the priority.

rules.factsNote: These are every fact a rule may consult. Widening the list is a code change with a review, not a row in a table.

chat.title: Ask
chat.detail: About your own figures. The assistant queries nothing on its own: it is handed your data and answers only from it.

off.title: The copilot is not switched on.
off.body: The provider and its key are not configured in this installation. Everything else works without it: the engine computes the figures, not the model.

threads.title: Conversations
threads.empty: You have not asked anything yet.

grounding.title: The figures it answered from
grounding.detail: What the assistant was given. Without this, an answer from three months ago would be impossible to check.

chat.ungrounded: This answer contains figures we could not verify against your data: {figures}

errors.copilotOff: The copilot is not switched on in this installation.
errors.createFailed: The conversation could not be saved.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

opening.knowTitle: Here is what I already know
opening.knowEmpty: I have almost nothing on you yet. Record an account and what is already committed, and this conversation will actually be worth having.
opening.askTitle: This I cannot know — tell me
opening.askDetail: Answer below, in your own words. What you tell me stays in this conversation and I take it into account in everything that follows.
opening.startersTitle: Or start with one of these
questions: What worries you most right now: getting to the end of the month, getting out of debt, or saving for something?
Is anything changing in the next few months — a big expense, a job change, somebody else in the house?

starters.surplus: I have {amount} left this month — what should I do with it?
starters.shortfall: I am {amount} short this month — what do I cut first?
starters.debt: Should I put everything into {name} before anything else?
starters.goal: Am I on track to reach «{name}»?
starters.budget: Why is the «{budget}» budget running away from me?
starters.month: How am I doing this month compared with normal?

composer.label: Your question
composer.placeholder: Ask a question, or tell me about your case…
composer.hint: Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line

chat.memory: It remembers everything said in this conversation. To start fresh, open a new one.

subscription.title: Your subscription
subscription.detail: What plan you are on, how much you have used, and what else exists.

usage.title: What you have used this month
usage.detail: Resets on the first of each month.

unavailable.title: Payment is not wired up here yet.
unavailable.body: This installation has no payment processor configured. Everything else works: the free plan's limits apply just the same.

subscription.provisional: Prices are provisional and will change before the first real charge.

errors.checkoutUnavailable: No payment processor is configured in this installation.
errors.checkoutFailed: The payment processor did not respond. Try again.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

access.title: Who gets into your household
access.detail: Your partner shares the money. Your accountant looks with permission, for a while. Those are not the same thing, and they are managed separately here.

notAllowed.title: Only the owner or their partner can hand out access.
notAllowed.body: Ask whoever created the household to raise your role if you need to invite people.

members.title: Members
members.detail: The people who sign in and see the household's money.
members.revokeConfirm: They stop getting in immediately. What they recorded is kept.

invite.title: Invite someone
invite.detail: A link is generated that expires in 7 days. It only works for the email address you enter.
invite.linkTitle: Done. Copy this link and send it to them:
invite.linkNote: We show it once. We do not store it in plain form: if you lose it, generate another invitation.

accountants.title: Accountant access
accountants.detail: With a scope and an expiry date.

errors.notAllowed: You do not have permission to do this.
errors.alreadyMember: That person is already in the household.
errors.cannotChangeOwner: The owner's role is not changed from here.
errors.cannotRemoveOwner: The owner's access is not removed.
errors.cannotRemoveSelf: You cannot remove your own access.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

accountants.title: Accountant access
accountants.detail: Somebody outside your household looking at your figures with a specific, revocable, dated permission.

grant.title: Grant access
grant.detail: Your accountant needs a Cifraapp account with that email. If they do not have one, invite them as a member first and then give them the right scope.
grant.expiresHint: In days. Put 0 for no expiry — though an access that lapses on its own beats one that relies on remembering.

list.title: Access granted
list.empty: You have not given anybody access yet.
list.revokeConfirm: They lose access immediately. The record that they had it is kept.

households.title: Your households
households.detail: If you manage more than one, this is where you choose which you are looking at.

create.title: Create another household
create.detail: A new one starts empty, with its own questionnaire.
create.name: Household name

errors.notFound: That household does not exist, or you no longer belong to it.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

invitation.title: You have been invited to a household
invitation.detail: Accepting means you will see that household's money, and they will see that you joined.

signInFirst.title: Sign in first.
signInFirst.body: The invitation is for a specific email address. Sign in with that address and open the link again.

errors.invalid: This link no longer works: it may have expired, or somebody already used it.
errors.wrongAccount: This invitation is for another email address. Sign in with that address and open the link again.
errors.signInRequired: Sign in and open the link again.

notifications.title: What we tell you
notifications.detail: A financial system that only speaks when opened is one nobody opens. This is yours, not the household's: your partner chooses their own.

kinds.commitmentDue: A commitment is about to fall due
kinds.commitmentDueDetail: And there is not enough in the account to cover it.
kinds.bufferNegativeDetail: What is committed went past what you have.
kinds.budgetPace: A category is on pace to go over
kinds.budgetPaceDetail: At the current rate, with the month not over.
kinds.importFinishedDetail: With how many movements are waiting for review.
kinds.reviewBacklog: There are decisions waiting for you
kinds.reviewBacklogDetail: Repeats, transfers or categories to confirm.
kinds.weeklySummaryDetail: What came in, what went out and what is coming.

log.title: What we sent you
log.detail: Including what we decided not to send, and why. «I never got it» has to have an answer.
log.empty: We have not sent you anything yet.

notifications.pending: Delivery is not connected in this installation yet. Your preferences are saved and will be honoured as soon as it is.

tax.title: Tax profile
tax.detail: For anyone invoicing on their own account. With this we can tell you how much to set aside from each invoice.

draftWarning.title: Panama's tax rules here are still a draft.
draftWarning.body: Nobody qualified has reviewed them, so the product shows you no figure computed from them. Saving your profile is still worth it: it is what will be used the day a Panamanian accountant reviews and publishes the rules, with their name and the date.

form.rucHint: Optional. We only store it; we look it up nowhere.
form.activityHint: What you do, in your own words.
form.methodHint: Cash is when you get paid; accrual is when you invoice.
form.fiscalYearHint: As MM-DD. If it is the calendar year, leave 01-01.

reserve.title: Tax reserve
reserve.detail: How much to set aside from each invoice.

remove.title: Remove the profile
remove.detail: If you stop invoicing on your own account.
remove.confirm: The profile is deleted. Your movements do not change.

taxReserve.title: Tax reserve
taxReserve.detail: The share of what you are paid that was never yours.

noProfile.title: You have no tax profile yet.
noProfile.body: Tell us how you are taxed and we can work out how much to set aside from each invoice.

notPublished.title: We cannot compute a figure for you yet.
notPublished.body: The Panamanian tax rules loaded here are an unreviewed draft. Showing you a number out of them would be worse than showing you nothing: a wrong balance is embarrassing, a wrong tax figure is a fine you pay.
notPublished.meanwhile: In the meantime you can use your own reserve rate in the household settings. It is yours and the product treats it as yours: it sets it aside, it does not compute it.

own.title: Your own rate
own.detail: The one you set in the settings. It is not a tax calculation, it is your decision.
own.onIncome: On what you have been paid this year
own.noRate: You have not set a reserve rate. Set one in the household settings and we will tell you how much to hold.

accounts.title: Where it is held
accounts.detail: Accounts of type «tax reserve». That is where the product looks for what you have set aside.
accounts.empty: You have no tax reserve account. Create one and move what you set aside into it: separating the money for real is what makes the reserve work.

scenarios.title: Scenarios
scenarios.detail: «What if I get a raise?» «What if we move?» Arithmetic on today's position, not a prediction.

list.title: Your scenarios
list.detail: Each one is recomputed from your current figures every time you open this screen.

scenarios.removeConfirm: The scenario is removed. Your figures do not change.

empty.title: No scenarios yet.
empty.body: Start with the one that keeps you up. «Rent goes up $150» and «I lose this contract for six months» are the two most common.

form.name: What are you asking?
form.nameHint: In your words. For example, «moving to San Francisco».
form.label: The change
form.labelHint: What you call it. For example, «higher rent».
form.startsHint: In months. 0 is from this month.
form.durationHint: In months. Leave it empty if it is permanent.

result.title: What changes
result.detail: Against doing nothing, at the end of the horizon.
result.shortfall: You run out of liquid money in {date}
result.noShortfall: You do not run out of liquid money inside the horizon
result.horizonNote: «You do not run out» is not reassurance: the horizon may simply be shorter than the problem.

projection.title: Projection
projection.detail: How the months ahead look if nothing changes. Arithmetic you could check on paper, not a forecast.

runway.title: Runway
runway.months: {count} months before you run out of liquid
runway.safe: You do not run out of liquid inside the horizon
runway.note: Not appearing here does not mean it does not happen: the horizon may be shorter than the problem.

empty.title: There is nothing to project from yet.
empty.body: It takes at least one account with a balance and one recorded income. With those we can show how the months ahead look.

assumptions.title: What this is computed on
assumptions.debts: {count} debts with their minimums and rates
assumptions.note: No new purchases, no inflation, no salary changes. If any of those are coming, look at Scenarios.

close.title: Month close
close.detail: Sealing a month is a promise: the figures you quoted from it will not change underneath you.

checklist.title: Before closing
checklist.detail: Two of these block the close. The others can be closed over, knowingly.

action.blocked: It cannot be closed yet: something blocking is outstanding.
action.confirm: After closing, correcting anything in this month requires reopening it and giving a reason.

history.title: Closed months
history.empty: You have not closed a month yet.

reopen.title: Reopen
reopen.detail: A reason is required, and it is kept. Somebody will ask why the figures you gave them changed.

errors.blockedByChecklist: Something blocking is still outstanding. Resolve it and come back.
errors.reasonRequired: Write why you are reopening it.
errors.signInRequired: Your session expired. Sign in again.

exports.title: Export
exports.detail: The same figures you see under Statements, in whatever format the person reading them needs.

kinds.transactionsDetail: Every movement in the period, with its category and account.
kinds.incomeDetail: What came in and what went out, grouped by category.

formats.csvDetail: Opens in any spreadsheet. Amounts go unformatted, so they are not read as text.
formats.xlsxDetail: With the types set: dates are dates and amounts are numbers. This is what an accountant asks for.
formats.pdfDetail: A document to send to a bank, a landlord or your accountant.
formats.jsonDetail: For another system. Carries the currency and the time it was generated.

exports.note: None of this is stored on the server. It is generated and sent: a financial export sitting in a bucket is a second copy of the most sensitive data here, kept for the convenience of a download that already worked.

investments.title: Investing
investments.detail: How much you would have to set aside each month to reach your goals, and what taking more risk actually buys you.

disclosure.title: Before you look at any figure on this screen
disclosure.body: This module **does not recommend what to invest in**, and it will not. Recommending a specific instrument is regulated advice, and this product does not give it. What it does is arithmetic: given your goals and a return assumption you can change, how much you would have to contribute each month. Returns are assumptions, not forecasts: nobody knows what markets will do, and any number here that looks like a promise is not one. Markets fall, and the table tells you how far mixes of this shape have historically fallen.

profile.title: Your profile
profile.detail: All of this you tell us. The module does not infer how much risk you can carry or how much you can set aside.
profile.risk: How much risk you are willing to carry
profile.riskHint: It describes a mix, not a product: how much sits in cash, in bonds and in broad equity.
profile.capacity: How much you can set aside each month
profile.capacityHint: What you are willing to leave alone, which is not the same as what is left over.
profile.interests: What you want to look at
profile.interestsHint: Comma separated. For example: energy, Panama bonds, technology. It feeds the explanation, never a recommendation.
profile.emergency: I already have an emergency fund
profile.emergencyHint: If you do not, that is the first goal, and we will say so before anything else.
profile.bandHint: Percent a year. Leave them empty to use the product's. If you think we are optimistic, lower them: they are assumptions, not data.
profile.usingDefault: You are using the product's assumptions.
profile.usingOwn: You are using your own assumptions.

risks.cashDetail: No equity. It does not fall, and it does not keep up with inflation either.
risks.growthDetail: Almost all broad equity. The most over decades, and the most painful along the way.

emergencyFirst.title: Before investing: the emergency fund.
emergencyFirst.body: You said you do not have one yet. Investing without a cushion forces a sale exactly when markets are down, which is the worst possible moment and also the likeliest one for an emergency. That is where the money goes first.

goals.title: What each goal would ask of you monthly
goals.detail: At each level's assumption. The no-growth column is the honest floor: what it would cost if markets did nothing for you.
goals.tooShort: Your horizon is shorter than this level suits
goals.drawdown: A fall of the historical size would take {amount} off along the way
goals.unreachable: This date cannot be met, whatever you contribute
goals.notAffordable: Does not fit in your {capacity} a month

empty.title: No goals with a date yet.
empty.body: Without a date there are no months, and without months there is no monthly figure. Put a date on a goal and this screen fills in.

goals.undated: No date, so nothing to model: {names}

narrative.title: What this means for you
narrative.detail: Written by the assistant over the figures above, and over what you said interests you. It names nothing to invest in, because it cannot.
narrative.unavailable: The copilot is not switched on in this installation. The figures above are exact regardless: the engine computes them.
narrative.budget: This month's assistant budget is spent. The figures are unaffected.
narrative.quality: The assistant returned a figure we could not verify against the modelling, so we did not show it. On this screen in particular that is exactly what should happen.
narrative.error: We could not reach the assistant. The figures are still exact.

watchlist.title: What you are watching
watchlist.detail: You put it here. The charts are TradingView's; the product neither stores nor interprets prices.
watchlist.symbolHint: The way TradingView writes it. For example NASDAQ:AAPL, AMEX:SPY or TVC:GOLD.
watchlist.label: What you call it
watchlist.removeConfirm: It leaves your list. Nothing else happens.

empty.title: Your list is empty.
empty.body: Add whatever you want to follow and its chart appears here. Something being on your list does not mean the product is proposing it.

watchlist.chartNote: Chart served by TradingView. Nothing it shows comes from your records.
watchlist.chartFailedBody: TradingView did not answer. It is usually an ad blocker, the network, or being offline. Nothing else on this screen depends on it: the modelling above is arithmetic on your own figures and consults no price.

portfolio.title: What you hold
portfolio.detail: Shares, funds and crypto you recorded. You state how much you hold; the market states the price, with the time it said it.
portfolio.noChange: No previous close to compare against yet.
portfolio.unpriced: Unpriced and left out of the total: {symbols}.
portfolio.provenance: Prices from {source}, stored with the moment they were taken. They are not live, and they are not recorded as though you had stated them: the quantity is yours, the price is the market’s.

empty.title: No shares or crypto recorded yet
empty.body: If you hold shares, funds or coins, add them in the questionnaire and they appear here with their value and their movement. Recording one is not a recommendation to buy it.
